top_news.title: Rajasthan CM Bhajanlal Sharma attends Shekhawati Heritage, Development Summit in Jaipur
top_news.summary: Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma on Saturday stated that the 'double-engine' government is ensuring the holistic development of the Shekhawati region by addressing the water crisis, improving connectivity, restoring historic havelis, and promoting tourism. He noted that, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of "Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi", the state government is not only preserving this heritage but also integrating it with tourism to create new employment opportunities. Furthermore, the government is working with a firm commitment to ensure the availability of water and electricity, enhance road connectivity, and boost investment. The Chief Minister was speaking at the 'Shekhawati Heritage and Development Summit' held in Jaipur on Saturday. Urging entrepreneurs to involve the younger generation in business and industry, the Chief Minister remarked that the hard work, skill, and entrepreneurial spirit of the people of Rajasthan are recognised worldwide. It is essential to encourage the youth and provide them with opportunities for entrepreneurship and job creation. He expressed confidence that through the collective efforts of the government, social organisations, entrepreneurs, local citizens, and the Shekhawati diaspora, the region will reach new milestones in development. Commending the office-bearers of the Shekhawati Foundation, those working toward heritage conservation, and the Rajasthani diaspora, the Chief Minister highlighted the vital role played by entrepreneurs and philanthropists (Bhamashahs) from the Shekhawati region in the nation's economic advancement. He noted that the Rajasthani diaspora, philanthropists, and social organisations have also diligently fulfilled their responsibilities through the 'Karmabhumi se Matrubhumi' (From Place of Work to Motherland) initiative. The Chief Minister stated that water is the state's most critical requirement. Prioritising this, the state government has entered into significant agreements, such as the 'Ram Jalsetu Link Project' and the Yamuna Water Agreement. He mentioned that out of the total proposed works worth approximately Rs 1 lakh crore under the Ram Jalsetu Link Project, projects worth about Rs 41,000 crores have already commenced. This initiative will facilitate the availability of water for irrigation, as well as meet drinking water and industrial needs. Rajasthan Chief Minister emphasised heritage conservation, tourism promotion, water security and improved connectivity to accelerate the region's development. He further explained that efforts are underway to address the water requirements of the Sikar, Churu, and Jhunjhunu districts through the Yamuna Water Agreement. Additionally, the government's efforts are expected to extend the benefits of the Narmada Water Agreement to regions including Barmer, Sanchore, Jalore, Bhinmal, and Raniwara. Furthermore, the state is working to meet the drinking water and irrigation needs of various regions through projects such as the Indira Gandhi Canal Project (IGNP), the Kishau Dam project, the Ferozepur Feeder, the Jawai Water Project, and other schemes. The Chief Minister stated that the state government is continuously working to increase power generation and achieve self-reliance in the energy sector. His administration has undertaken comprehensive efforts to boost electricity production. Farmers and hotel operators are also being encouraged to adopt solar energy. Achieving self-reliance in the energy sector will accelerate industrial development, attract investment, and foster job creation. The Chief Minister stated that road connectivity plays a crucial role in the economic progress of any region. With this objective, work is underway on road projects such as the Kotputli-Kishangarh Greenfield Expressway and the Bikaner-Kotputli Expressway. These projects will directly connect Sikar, Jhunjhunu, and Churu to the national highway network. Furthermore, travel between Delhi-NCR and Western Rajasthan will become significantly more convenient. This will facilitate the transportation and marketing of agricultural produce, reduce costs, and provide a boost to industrial activities as well as religious and cultural tourism. He noted that the heritage of Shekhawati is not limited merely to its havelis (traditional mansions); rather, every element here holds historical significance. The government endeavours to integrate these havelis into tourism-related activities while ensuring the preservation of their original architectural character and traditional artwork. He added that the historical havelis and cultural heritage of Shekhawati offer immense potential for the growth of the hotel and tourism industry. The state government is currently working on the conservation of 662 havelis across the Shekhawati region. The Chief Minister said that work is also being done to develop a heritage tourism circuit including Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Churu. Local artists and artisans doing painting and traditional craft work in Havelis will be linked to this campaign by providing skill training. With this, our traditional art will be safe and local youth will get new employment opportunities. The Chief Minister also called upon the residents of the area to take active participation in the preservation of their historical havelis and heritage. Referring to the Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit, the Chief Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, an investment-friendly environment is being created in Rajasthan to realise the resolve of a developed India. Groundbreaking of investment agreements worth over Rs 9 lakh crore out of approximately Rs 35 lakh crore has been completed through the Rising Rajasthan Investment Summit. The priority of the government is to bring the investment to the ground and deliver its benefits to the common people. Private investment can also play an important role in the Shekhawati region, which will enable better utilisation of local resources and expansion of economic activities. The Chief Minister said that our government is moving towards development by preserving the heritage. He said that the Shekhawati Heritage Meet will be organised on December 8 to promote the historical heritage, havelis and tourism of Shekhawati. Its objective is to connect the Shekhawati migrants settled in the country and abroad with the preservation of the heritage of their motherland, tourism development and investment opportunities. On this occasion, MLA Gopal Sharma, National President of Shekhawati Foundation Vinod Goyal, National Convenor Hari Sharma, National General Secretary Gajanand Sharma, National Incharge Girdhari Kaishot and other officials of the Foundation, including a large number of people of Shekhawati region, were present. (ANI)

top_news.title: "Considering offering lower fares for travel on Golden Chariot in off-season": Karnataka CM Shivakumar
top_news.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said the state government is considering offering lower fares for travel on the luxury Golden Chariot train during the off-season to ensure that common people can also experience the state's historical, cultural and natural heritage. Speaking to the media at Majestic and Kengeri railway stations, Shivakumar said the initiative aims to promote Karnataka's tourist destinations, introduce new spots and create employment opportunities. "Through the Golden Chariot, we aim to introduce Karnataka's tourist spots to the public and create employment. We do not need a profit from this. However, there should be no loss," he said, seeking everyone's support for the initiative. The Chief Minister said the Tourism Department's 'Karnataka Darshana' scheme had been halted earlier but was revamped and restarted after the government came to power, with Tourism Minister KJ George taking charge. "The Tourism Department's 'Karnataka Darshana' scheme had been halted in between. After our government came to power and Minister K.J. George took charge, he revamped it and restarted the prestigious 'Golden Chariot'. New tourist routes have been set, and luxury amenities have been provided. Already, 75 passengers are travelling. Those who have not seen Karnataka completely should be encouraged to travel. For that purpose, the state government built special railway coaches and restarted the project by utilising the Railway Department's routes," he stated. articles.title: Rajasthan CM Bhajanlal Sharma attends Shekhawati Heritage, Development Summit in Jaipur
articles.summary: Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma on Saturday stated that the 'double-engine' government is ensuring the holistic development of the Shekhawati region by addressing the water crisis, improving connectivity, restoring historic havelis, and promoting tourism. He noted that, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of "Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi", the state government is not only preserving this heritage but also integrating it with tourism to create new employment opportunities. Furthermore, the government is working with a firm commitment to ensure the availability of water and electricity, enhance road connectivity, and boost investment. The Chief Minister was speaking at the 'Shekhawati Heritage and Development Summit' held in Jaipur on Saturday. Urging entrepreneurs to involve the younger generation in business and industry, the Chief Minister remarked that the hard work, skill, and entrepreneurial spirit of the people of Rajasthan are recognised worldwide. It is essential to encourage the youth and provide them with opportunities for entrepreneurship and job creation. He expressed confidence that through the collective efforts of the government, social organisations, entrepreneurs, local citizens, and the Shekhawati diaspora, the region will reach new milestones in development. Commending the office-bearers of the Shekhawati Foundation, those working toward heritage conservation, and the Rajasthani diaspora, the Chief Minister highlighted the vital role played by entrepreneurs and philanthropists (Bhamashahs) from the Shekhawati region in the nation's economic advancement. He noted that the Rajasthani diaspora, philanthropists, and social organisations have also diligently fulfilled their responsibilities through the 'Karmabhumi se Matrubhumi' (From Place of Work to Motherland) initiative. The Chief Minister stated that water is the state's most critical requirement. Prioritising this, the state government has entered into significant agreements, such as the 'Ram Jalsetu Link Project' and the Yamuna Water Agreement. He mentioned that out of the total proposed works worth approximately Rs 1 lakh crore under the Ram Jalsetu Link Project, projects worth about Rs 41,000 crores have already commenced. This initiative will facilitate the availability of water for irrigation, as well as meet drinking water and industrial needs. Rajasthan Chief Minister emphasised heritage conservation, tourism promotion, water security and improved connectivity to accelerate the region's development. He further explained that efforts are underway to address the water requirements of the Sikar, Churu, and Jhunjhunu districts through the Yamuna Water Agreement. Additionally, the government's efforts are expected to extend the benefits of the Narmada Water Agreement to regions including Barmer, Sanchore, Jalore, Bhinmal, and Raniwara. Furthermore, the state is working to meet the drinking water and irrigation needs of various regions through projects such as the Indira Gandhi Canal Project (IGNP), the Kishau Dam project, the Ferozepur Feeder, the Jawai Water Project, and other schemes. The Chief Minister stated that the state government is continuously working to increase power generation and achieve self-reliance in the energy sector. His administration has undertaken comprehensive efforts to boost electricity production. Farmers and hotel operators are also being encouraged to adopt solar energy. Achieving self-reliance in the energy sector will accelerate industrial development, attract investment, and foster job creation. The Chief Minister stated that road connectivity plays a crucial role in the economic progress of any region. With this objective, work is underway on road projects such as the Kotputli-Kishangarh Greenfield Expressway and the Bikaner-Kotputli Expressway. These projects will directly connect Sikar, Jhunjhunu, and Churu to the national highway network. Furthermore, travel between Delhi-NCR and Western Rajasthan will become significantly more convenient. This will facilitate the transportation and marketing of agricultural produce, reduce costs, and provide a boost to industrial activities as well as religious and cultural tourism. He noted that the heritage of Shekhawati is not limited merely to its havelis (traditional mansions); rather, every element here holds historical significance. The government endeavours to integrate these havelis into tourism-related activities while ensuring the preservation of their original architectural character and traditional artwork. He added that the historical havelis and cultural heritage of Shekhawati offer immense potential for the growth of the hotel and tourism industry. The state government is currently working on the conservation of 662 havelis across the Shekhawati region. The Chief Minister said that work is also being done to develop a heritage tourism circuit including Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Churu. Local artists and artisans doing painting and traditional craft work in Havelis will be linked to this campaign by providing skill training. With this, our traditional art will be safe and local youth will get new employment opportunities. The Chief Minister also called upon the residents of the area to take active participation in the preservation of their historical havelis and heritage. Referring to the Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit, the Chief Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, an investment-friendly environment is being created in Rajasthan to realise the resolve of a developed India. Groundbreaking of investment agreements worth over Rs 9 lakh crore out of approximately Rs 35 lakh crore has been completed through the Rising Rajasthan Investment Summit. The priority of the government is to bring the investment to the ground and deliver its benefits to the common people. Private investment can also play an important role in the Shekhawati region, which will enable better utilisation of local resources and expansion of economic activities. The Chief Minister said that our government is moving towards development by preserving the heritage. He said that the Shekhawati Heritage Meet will be organised on December 8 to promote the historical heritage, havelis and tourism of Shekhawati. Its objective is to connect the Shekhawati migrants settled in the country and abroad with the preservation of the heritage of their motherland, tourism development and investment opportunities. On this occasion, MLA Gopal Sharma, National President of Shekhawati Foundation Vinod Goyal, National Convenor Hari Sharma, National General Secretary Gajanand Sharma, National Incharge Girdhari Kaishot and other officials of the Foundation, including a large number of people of Shekhawati region, were present. (ANI)

articles.title: "Considering offering lower fares for travel on Golden Chariot in off-season": Karnataka CM Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said the state government is considering offering lower fares for travel on the luxury Golden Chariot train during the off-season to ensure that common people can also experience the state's historical, cultural and natural heritage. Speaking to the media at Majestic and Kengeri railway stations, Shivakumar said the initiative aims to promote Karnataka's tourist destinations, introduce new spots and create employment opportunities. "Through the Golden Chariot, we aim to introduce Karnataka's tourist spots to the public and create employment. We do not need a profit from this. However, there should be no loss," he said, seeking everyone's support for the initiative. The Chief Minister said the Tourism Department's 'Karnataka Darshana' scheme had been halted earlier but was revamped and restarted after the government came to power, with Tourism Minister KJ George taking charge. "The Tourism Department's 'Karnataka Darshana' scheme had been halted in between. After our government came to power and Minister K.J. George took charge, he revamped it and restarted the prestigious 'Golden Chariot'. New tourist routes have been set, and luxury amenities have been provided. Already, 75 passengers are travelling. Those who have not seen Karnataka completely should be encouraged to travel. For that purpose, the state government built special railway coaches and restarted the project by utilising the Railway Department's routes," he stated. Shivakumar said the government had also formulated a tourist circuit, 'Jewels of the South', connecting destinations including Hampi, Mahabalipuram, Mysuru, Bengaluru, Cochin and Chettinad. A four-day tour package, 'Dreams of Karnataka', has also been prepared, with details to be shared in the coming days. "Not just this, with the aim of introducing South Indian destinations, we have formulated another tourist circuit called 'Jewels of the South'. We have prepared a route connecting great tourist centres like Hampi, Mahabalipuram, Mysuru, Bengaluru, Cochin, Chettinad, and others. A four-day tour package named 'Dreams of Karnataka' is also ready. Information regarding this will be provided in the coming days," he said. Highlighting the facilities on the Golden Chariot, he said the train has two restaurants with seating for around 80 passengers, while nearly 60 staff members serve travellers. It also offers facilities such as a spa, gym, vegetarian and non-vegetarian dining options, and overnight accommodation. "The Golden Chariot train features two restaurants. There is seating for about 80 passengers, and nearly 60 staff members work to serve them. There are many facilities including a spa, gym, and vegetarian and non-vegetarian dining options. Excellent arrangements have also been made for a comfortable overnight stay. I was very pleased to see everything. I too am waiting for an opportunity to travel on this train," he said. "This train is a valuable asset to Karnataka's tourism. Re-launching this train, which could not be utilised properly in the past, and making it run on routes that attract tourists will complement the growth of tourism," he said, expressing confidence. Calling the train the pride of Karnataka, Shivakumar said it should not remain accessible only to wealthy travellers or tourists from other states. The government is exploring lower fares to enable more people from Karnataka to experience the luxury train, and discussions have also been held with the Railway Department. "This train should not be restricted only to tourists from other states. People of our Karnataka should also take advantage of it in large numbers. Discussions have also been held with the Railway Department in this regard," he said. He added that the service is being developed in collaboration with the Karnataka Tourism Department, Indian Railways and IRCTC, and is expected to support local economic activities, including the hotel industry at tourist destinations. On expanding the train's routes, Shivakumar said officials from the state tourism and railway departments would discuss suitable options without disrupting regular train services. Separately, responding to a question about tourists from Karnataka stranded in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, he said he had written to the Central Government and was in contact with the External Affairs Minister regarding the matter. "I have requested flight arrangements/security if needed. There are technical issues with flight operations," he said, adding that a helpline had been established for Kannadigas and that state officials were in continuous contact. "No one needs to panic. Our government, along with the Minorities Department and the Central Government, is with you," the Chief Minister said. (ANI)
